title: Investigation of the reactive balance ability of elderly people using a perturbation treadmill
summary:
Background
Falls are a major problem in old age, as they often lead to serious injuries and restrict independence. When people lose their balance, a rapid and correct compensatory movement of the feet (a so-called step reaction) is crucial to prevent a fall. To date, there are few simple ways to reliably train these automatic protective reactions in everyday clinical practice.

Objective
Through special tests on a particular treadmill that triggers targeted balance disturbances, the study aims to investigate how older adults react to sudden instability.

Method
Older adults participate in the study. In a single appointment, various mobility tests are performed, and the reaction to balance disturbances on the special treadmill is measured. Additionally, the participants maintain a calendar over a period of one year, in which they record every fall.

interventions.name: Performance of step-reaction tests and mobility assessments during a single appointment, and recording of falls after 3 and 12 months using a fall calendar.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
CHARMI® ≥ 6
mobile at room level without assistive devices
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients in a palliative care situation (life expectancy < 3 months based on clinical assessment by medical staff).
• Patients lacking the capacity to consent (e.g., known advanced dementia).
• Assessments not possible due to impaired communication skills (e.g., due to lack of language proficiency).
• Inability to walk on the treadmill at habitual walking speed for 2 minutes.
• Uncontrolled cardiovascular, metabolic, or psychiatric disorders.
• Presence of a permanent infusion or continuous use of an oxygen device.
• Body weight exceeding 135 kg.
• Severe osteoporosis.
• Currently existing bone fractures.
• Open or chronic wounds.
• Surgical interventions within the last eight weeks (including closed reduction of, e.g., joint replacements).
